title: Incremental PII eviction index and query gate for analytics stores
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Analytics event stores and downstream materialized views can contain PII (identified by user_id, email, session payloads). Current bulk deletion/backfill approaches are operationally expensive and cause large reprocessing windows. We need an online, incremental mechanism to ensure tenant-scoped PII is quickly excluded from query results, and that deletions are provable and auditable without full dataset rewrites.

Proposal: Build an Incremental PII Eviction Index (IPEI) plus a query-time gate for analytics reads. The IPEI is a compact, append-only store of tombstones keyed by tenant and data shard that supports fast membership checks. Deletion workflow: 1) API request or erasure job writes tombstones to IPEI with provenance metadata and retention window; 2) streaming job fanout propagates tombstones to materialized-view invalidation queues and update markers for incremental aggregations; 3) query gateway consults IPEI as a low-latency membership filter to exclude matching rows at read time; 4) background reconciler compacts IPEI and schedules physical removal/backfills for persisted aggregates on an operator schedule.

Why incremental: avoids full re-ingest of historical events for immediate compliance; supports low-latency customer-visible deletion while backfills run asynchronously; provides an auditable append-only trail for legal attestation.
acceptance_criteria: Writing a tenant-scoped tombstone to the IPEI causes subsequent analytic queries for that tenant to exclude affected rows within 30s in staging
IPEI supports >10k tombstones/sec ingest for peak backfill bursts without dropping membership checks
Audit export includes tombstone provenance (request ID, initiating user, retention policy, timestamp) and passes the compliance checklist
Background reconciler can compact tombstones older than configured retention and schedule physical row deletions/backfills according to policy
Query-time gate latency impact is <3ms p50 and <8ms p95 added to typical analytics read path
End-to-end test coverage and a runbook for emergency rollback are added before release
implementation_notes: Data model: tombstone key = <tenant_id>::<shard_id>::<hashed_subject_id>; value = JSON blob (provenance, request_id, erase_type, origin_service, created_at)
Store choice: start with DynamoDB for predictable point-read latency and TTL support; evaluate RocksDB-on-EC2 as cheaper alternative for Dedicated customers
Streaming: use existing console analytics Kafka topic with a tombstone topic and consumer group that fans out invalidation messages to view updaters and query cache invalidators

Query gate: add a configurable middleware in analytics read service that batches membership checks to IPEI (prefetch for top-1000 subjects per query) and falls back to cached negative set for short windows
Compaction: compaction worker merges tombstones, emits compacted manifests to S3 for audit exports, and publishes physical deletion tasks to the batch backfill queue
Backfills: schedule low-priority physical row deletions per tenant; provide operator flags for emergency expedite; ensure idempotency markers to avoid double-deletions
Security: tombstone payloads must be encrypted at rest with KMS, access-controlled (only privacy team + ops), and surfaced in audit logs
Metrics & observability: ingest rate, membership latency histogram, tombstones_pending_for_backfill gauge, compaction lag, query_gate_error_rate; add dashboard and alert thresholds
Testing: unit tests for membership logic, integration tests against a local DynamoDB emulator, staged load test simulating 50k tombstones/min bursts
Performance: evaluate batched membership checks to reduce per-request RPCs; implement local LRU cache with TTL tuned to 60s for high-frequency subjects

2026-03-05 - Security review request filed (SEC-2026-042). Security requested key-rotation plan and more strict RBAC on tombstone reads; blocking until doc updated.
2026-03-07 - Prototype: DynamoDB-backed IPEI writer + local query gate implemented in feature branch. Initial microbench shows 2ms p50 membership checks for single-key reads.
